# The Sky's Ancient Scroll

## Scripture
"The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands. Day after day they pour forth speech; night after night they reveal knowledge." — Psalm 19:1-2

## Reflection
On a late August evening, as the last blush of sunset fades, the sky becomes a scroll unfurling ancient wisdom. The stars of Cygnus, the Swan, glide along the Milky Way like ink strokes on parchment—testimony written long before any human alphabet existed.

Psalm 19 paints the heavens not as a silent backdrop but as a voice—one that speaks without words yet communicates with unrelenting clarity. Every night, the same constellations rise, not because the universe is mechanical, but because our God is faithful. The stars don't wonder whether they should shine; they simply obey the One who spoke them into being.

We live in a noisy world—notifications, opinions, endless chatter. Yet under the open sky, we remember: God's first language to humanity wasn't a book, but a canvas. The sky is his ongoing sermon, proclaiming that the same God who positioned Arcturus and bound the Pleiades holds your anxious heart in steady hands.

When our internal skies grow cloudy with doubt, the external sky reminds us that light persists—faithfully, patiently, night after night.

## Prayer
Lord of the heavens, teach us to read the sky as your unspoken Word. When our days feel chaotic, let the ordered stars remind us of your steadfast nature. May we trust your voice even when we cannot hear it, and rest in the knowledge that you who set the stars in place are holding us close. Amen.
